newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: RTZ-CRA mulling Argentine gold data.
newsitem.headline: RTZ-CRA mulling Argentine gold data.

text.p: Anglo-Australian mining giant RTZ Plc-CRA Ltd is evaluating advanced exploration results at its Famatina gold prospect in northwestern Argentina, the firm's Argentine Exploration Manager Timothy Beale said.
"We are currently evaluating a large amount of information related to the project in order to determine how we wish to proceed," Beale told Reuters in a telephone interview.
Asked whether the project was nearing feasibility study phase, he replied, "It's too early to say...I think there's more advanced exploration to be done."

He said significant drilling had been done at the site in the Famatina mountains in the center of La Rioja province, even though none was going on at the moment. While the prospect's main interest was gold, there was "a certain amount of copper as well."
Beales would not specify how much drilling had been done at the site, what exactly the results had been, nor what RTZ-CRA was budgeting for Famatina.

The main part of the prospect is at high altitude, about 16,000 feet (4,800 meters) above sea-level. Despite some problems with high winds, snow and cold during winter, the site is usually accessible all year round.
RTZ-CRA has taken an option on the property from its Argentine owners, Beale said.
The firm is also looking for copper and gold in several other areas in western and northwestern Argentina, Beale said, but Famatina is its most advanced project in the country.
